title: Somerset's 'most haunted' pubs with monks, spirits and spooky goings-on
excerpt: From mysterious monks to resident spirits, these Somerset pubs have gained spooky reputations for their reported paranormal activity
content:
Somerset has no shortage of historic pubs, but some are said to have more than just drinkers passing through their doors.

Across the county, landlords and customers have reported unexplained noises, mysterious figures and other supposed paranormal encounters.

Some pubs have developed particularly spooky reputations over the years.

Here are some of Somerset's allegedly haunted watering holes.

The Vivary Arms in Taunton has a spooky reputation (Image: The Vivary Arms)

Vivary Arms, Taunton

The Vivary Arms in Taunton hit the headlines after its landlords reported a series of mysterious occurrences.

Kat and Martin Bowden told the Somerset County Gazette in 2020 they believed the pub was being haunted by the ghost of a former monk.

Kat reported seeing a cloaked figure near the toilets, while the couple said they had experienced doors slamming, objects disappearing and bottles and glasses apparently moving overnight.

They also claimed lights and a fruit machine had switched on unexpectedly.

Janie and Nigel Deeming (Image: SWNS)

Stags Head Inn, Dunster

The centuries-old Stags Head Inn in Dunster has its own tales of paranormal activity.

Janie and Nigel Deeming, who were run the 15th-century pub, told the Somerset County Gazette in 2023 it had a "resident ghost".

Janie said nearly every building in Dunster was believed to have "a ghost or two", with the historic village surrounded by supernatural stories.

Somerset's association with pub-based ghost stories continues today. 

A Halloween tour running in October 2026 is visiting the Alhampton Inn, Eli's Rose and Crown in Huish Episcopi, Old Down Inn in Chilcompton and The Flying Fish near Ilminster.

Organiser Luke Knight said he had been told some of the venues even had "a ghost or two", although he did not reveal which ones.
